# Booklet

> Publish clean, readable pages from Markdown — by hand, by script, or by your AI assistant.

Booklet turns Markdown into a shareable page with one link. Paste or write Markdown, watch it render live, hit Publish, get a URL back. No account required to try it.

## What Booklet does

- Converts Markdown into a formatted, readable web page with a permanent public URL
- Renders GitHub-Flavored Markdown — headings, code blocks, tables, lists, task lists, blockquotes — plus KaTeX math, Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams, callouts (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!CAUTION]`), collapsible toggle sections, and multi-column layouts
- Auto-generates a table of contents once a document has enough headings
- Reads YAML frontmatter: `title`, `slug`, `visibility`, `description`, `author`, `date`, `tags`
- Live preview in the browser editor as you type
- Multiple named drafts, autosaved locally in the browser
- 21 built-in templates (incident report, ADR, runbook, release notes, postmortem, and more — full list below)
- Export a published page to Markdown, HTML, or PDF
- Per-page analytics: views, read depth, referrers (signed-in only)
- Version history: restore any of the last 50 versions of a page (signed-in only)
- Password-protected pages (signed-in only)
- Custom URL slugs (signed-in only)
- Team spaces: a shared collection of pages under one URL, with invited members

## REST API

All endpoints are under `/api/v1/`, authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer <bklt_...>`:

- `POST /api/v1/publish` — create a new page, returns `{ id, url }`
- `PATCH /api/v1/pages/{id}` — update an existing page in place (same URL)
- `GET /api/v1/pages` — list pages owned by the authenticated account, with `q`/`tag` filters
- `GET /api/v1/pages/{id}` — read a page's metadata and raw Markdown
- `DELETE /api/v1/pages/{id}` — delete a page permanently

API keys are generated from the My Pages dashboard after signing in (free).

Full reference: https://booklet.ashwinsathian.com/api-docs

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Booklet runs a native MCP server so Claude and other MCP-compatible AI assistants can publish and manage pages directly, in the same conversation.

MCP endpoint: `https://booklet-mcp.ashwinsathian.com/mcp` (remote, Streamable HTTP — nothing to install)
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <bklt_...>` header, same API key as the REST API

**Tools:** `publish_page`, `update_page`, `get_page`, `list_pages`, `delete_page`
**Resources:** published pages, browsable and readable as `booklet://pages/:id`
**Prompts:** five pre-built document templates the assistant can fill in and publish directly — `incident_report`, `adr`, `release_notes`, `rfc`, `runbook`

Setup instructions (Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed): https://booklet.ashwinsathian.com/mcp-setup

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "booklet": {
      "url": "https://booklet-mcp.ashwinsathian.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## CLI

```
npx booklet-cli publish README.md
```

Or install it globally: `npm install -g booklet-cli`. Supports non-interactive auth (`--key` / `BOOKLET_API_KEY`) for CI, `--update <id>` to republish a page in place, `--watch` for auto-republish on save, and shell completion.

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/booklet-cli

## GitHub Action

`AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet` publishes a Markdown file to Booklet from a CI workflow and returns the URL as a step output:

```yaml
- uses: AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet@v1
  with:
    file: CHANGELOG.md
    api-key: ${{ secrets.BOOKLET_API_KEY }}
```

Repository: https://github.com/AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet

## Pricing

Free, permanently — there is no paid tier. Anonymous publishing needs no account and is capped at 10 pages per month per IP address, with no expiry on the pages themselves. Signing in is also free and removes that cap entirely, while unlocking custom slugs, analytics, version history, password protection, API access, and webhooks. Every published page carries a small "Published via Booklet" attribution that stays on regardless of plan — there's no option to remove it.

## Technical details

- Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- Self-hosted MongoDB; the app runs as a single process behind a Cloudflare Tunnel
- No user content is used for training or resold
- XSS-safe: content renders through a custom block-based AST renderer, never as raw injected HTML

## Templates available

Incident Report, Architecture Decision Record (ADR), Release Notes, README, Meeting Notes, Onboarding Guide, Runbook, Postmortem, Weekly Update, Product Spec, Design Review, API Changelog, Technical Investigation, Sprint Retrospective, Job Description, Interview Debrief, Project Kickoff, Launch Checklist, Data Dictionary, Proposal, User Research Report
